paragraphs.title: The Deposition of Jehoahaz and the Rise of Jehoiakim

easy.explanation: The people of the land took Jehoahaz and made him king in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz reigned three months in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How long did Jehoahaz reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The king of Egypt put Jehoahaz down at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who put Jehoahaz down from the throne?

answers: He imposed a fine on the land and made Jehoiakim king
medium.explanation: The king of Egypt condemned the land and made Eliakim, later called Jehoiakim, king.
medium.q: What did the king of Egypt do after removing Jehoahaz?

answers: The king of Egypt changed his name
medium.explanation: The king of Egypt turned Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim.
Nebuchadnezzar bound Jehoiakim in fetters in order to carry him to Babylon.
medium.q: What does “bound him in fetters” mean?

answers: Jehoahaz, then Jehoiakim, and afterward Jehoiachin
Jehoiakim, then Jehoahaz, and afterward Zedekiah
Jehoiachin, then Jehoahaz, and afterward Jehoiakim
challenge.explanation: The people made Jehoahaz king, Egypt made Jehoiakim king, and Jehoiakim's son Jehoiachin followed him.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the changes in Judah's kingship?

answers: He carried its vessels to Babylon
He commanded it to be rebuilt
challenge.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar carried the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his temple.
challenge.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do concerning the house of the LORD?

answers: He did what was good in the sight of the LORD
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Jehoiakim did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD his God.
challenge.q: What trait of Jehoiakim is emphasized?

paragraphs.title: Jehoiachin and Zedekiah under Babylonian Rule

easy.explanation: Jehoiachin reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How long did Jehoiachin reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought Jehoiachin to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar made Zedekiah, Jehoiachin's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar make king after Jehoiachin?

medium.explanation: Zedekiah reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
Zedekiah humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet.
medium.q: Before whom did Zedekiah not humble himself?

answers: He rose up against the king
medium.explanation: Zedekiah rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God.
medium.q: What does “he also rebelled” mean in this passage?

answers: Babylon removed kings and appointed others in their place
Babylon allowed Judah to choose all its kings
Babylon did not interfere with Judah's kings
challenge.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin away and appointed Zedekiah in his place.
challenge.q: What do these verses show about Babylon's control over Judah?

answers: He broke the oath he had made
He carried away the vessels of the Temple
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah rebelled against the king who had made him swear by God.
challenge.q: Besides refusing to humble himself before Jeremiah, what else did Zedekiah do?

answers: He reigned three months and ten days
He reigned until the Persian kingdom
challenge.explanation: The passage gives his brief reign as three months and ten days.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Jehoiachin's reign was especially short?

paragraphs.title: The People's Sins and Rejected Warnings

answers: The chief of the priests and the people
The king of Egypt and his soldiers
easy.explanation: The chief of the priests and the people transgressed and polluted the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Who polluted the house of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD sent messengers and prophets to them.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD send to the people?

answers: They mocked and despised the messengers
They immediately went up to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: They mocked God's messengers, despised his words, and misused his prophets.
easy.q: How did the people respond to the warnings?

answers: Because he had compassion on his people and dwelling place
Because he wanted to make Pharaoh king
Because he wanted to take the Temple vessels
medium.explanation: The LORD sent them because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
medium.q: Why did the LORD repeatedly send his messengers?

answers: They immediately received a new king
The wrath of the LORD arose until there was no remedy
medium.explanation: Their rejection continued until the wrath of the LORD arose and there was no remedy.
medium.q: What happened after the people continued in sin and rejected the warnings?

answers: They committed repeated violations and acts of unfaithfulness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the people's many serious sins and unfaithfulness toward God.
medium.q: What does “transgressed very much” mean in this context?

answers: The people sinned, rejected warnings, and finally had no remedy
The people obeyed the prophets, so the Temple was built
The people went to Babylon, so prophets were sent to them
challenge.explanation: The passage connects persistent sin and rejection of warnings with the final judgment.

answers: He acted with compassion and gave repeated warnings
He had no concern for the people
He wanted to remove the prophets
challenge.explanation: The LORD repeatedly sent messengers because he had compassion on his people.
challenge.q: What does the repeated sending of prophets reveal about the LORD?

answers: The chief of the priests and the people
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically names the chief of the priests and the people.
challenge.q: Who is specifically included among those who sinned?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem and the Exile

easy.explanation: The LORD brought upon Judah the king of the Chaldees.
The Chaldeans burned the house of God.
easy.q: What did the Chaldeans do to the house of God?

easy.explanation: Those who escaped the sword were carried away to Babylon.

medium.explanation: The passage says that they broke down the wall of Jerusalem.
medium.q: What did the Chaldeans do to the wall of Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The vessels and treasures of the house of God, the king, and the princes were brought to Babylon.
medium.q: What was taken from the house of God, the king's house, and the princes' houses?

answers: It rested and ceased from its labor
medium.explanation: The desolate land rested during the years in which it was deprived of its normal activity.
medium.q: What does “she kept sabbath” mean concerning the land?

challenge.explanation: The land kept sabbath to fulfill threescore and ten years, or seventy years.
challenge.q: How long did the land rest according to the passage?

answers: Exile, rebuilding the wall, and then burning the Temple
Burning the Temple, breaking down the wall, and taking the treasures to Babylon
Building the Temple, gathering treasures, and then exile
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the burning of God's house, the breaking of Jerusalem's wall, and the removal of its treasures.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Jerusalem's destruction?

answers: The king of Babylon and his sons
challenge.explanation: The survivors were servants to the king of Babylon and his sons until the reign of Persia.
challenge.q: To whom were the survivors servants?

paragraphs.title: Cyrus's Proclamation and the Beginning of Redemption

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia.”
easy.q: In which year of Cyrus's reign did these events occur?

easy.explanation: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia.
easy.q: Who stirred up the spirit of Cyrus?

answers: A house for the LORD in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Cyrus said that the LORD had charged him to build a house in Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Cyrus say he was charged to build?

medium.explanation: Cyrus made a proclamation throughout his kingdom and put it in writing.
medium.q: How did Cyrus make his proclamation known?

answers: The king of Babylon gave him the land
The LORD had given him all the kingdoms of the earth
medium.explanation: Cyrus declared that the LORD God of heaven had given him all the kingdoms of the earth.
medium.q: What did Cyrus say about the source of his authority?

answers: Let him return or travel up to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Cyrus invited the people of the LORD to go up to Jerusalem and build the house.
medium.q: What does “let him go up” mean in the final verse?

answers: Cyrus's proclamation fulfilled the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the proclamation took place so that the word spoken by Jeremiah might be accomplished.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Cyrus's proclamation and Jeremiah's words?

answers: The way opens for the people to return and rebuild the house of the LORD
The people's slavery in Babylon becomes worse
challenge.explanation: Cyrus invites the people to go up, opening the way toward restoration and rebuilding.
challenge.q: What major change occurs at the end of the chapter?

answers: Any of the people of the LORD among them
Only the chief of the priests
challenge.explanation: Cyrus asked, “Who is there among you of all his people?” and invited them to go up.
challenge.q: Who did Cyrus invite to go up?
